s0001: Why did the Aral Sea dry up?
s0002:
Scenario. Geographer Dilnoza Rahimova is coming to your school to give a talk about her field research on the shores of the Aral Sea. To prepare for the talk, you are reading three sources.

SOURCE 1. A professor's blog — “A Geographer's Diary” (geographersdiary.uz/field/moynaq)

May 23, 11:22
This morning I looked out of the window of the house I am renting in Moynaq. In the distance, a salt flat lies white, saxaul and camelthorn bushes sway in the wind, the sky is clear, and on the horizon you can see the steep cliffs of the Ustyurt Plateau.

I feel a little sad, knowing this is my last week here. I have finished my fieldwork and will soon return to Tashkent. Later today I will go to the ship graveyard on the edge of town to say goodbye to the rusting ships I have studied for the past nine months.

If you have been following my blog, you know that Moynaq was once a busy port. In the 1960s, a fish cannery operated here, and boats went out to sea every day. Today the water is more than 100 kilometers from the town.

For many years, tourists who came to Moynaq wondered how the ships ended up sitting on the sand. Some thought a powerful storm had thrown them onto land. In the 1990s, a group of geographers, together with local fishermen, compared old maps and satellite images and showed that the ships had not moved at all; instead, the water had retreated away from them. That is how the mystery of the ships was solved.

However, another mystery still remains. Why did the sea dry up almost completely in such a short time — in only half a century? When I look out of my window, where waves once broke I see only sand and salt. We will explore this puzzle in my next posts and talks. For now, I suggest you start with Akmal Nurmatov's book “The Dried-Up Sea.” This review of the book is a good place to begin.

Comments:
Traveler_14 (May 24, 16:31): Hello, professor! I read your posts about the Aral with great interest. I can't wait to read “The Dried-Up Sea”!
AralFan_KB (May 25, 09:07): I really like your observations about the Aral. But I think another theory should also be considered. Try reading this article: sciencenow.uz/aral-climate

SOURCE 2. Book review — “The Dried-Up Sea” (bookreviews.uz)

Akmal Nurmatov's new book, “The Dried-Up Sea,” is a serious warning about what happens when people treat nature carelessly. The book describes several lakes and rivers that have changed dramatically because of human activity. One of the most tragic examples in the book is the Aral Sea.

The author writes that in 1960 the Aral was the fourth-largest lake in the world, with an area of almost 68 thousand square kilometers. The sea fed thousands of fishermen, and port towns such as Moynaq and Aralsk flourished. Starting in the 1960s, a large part of the water of the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers was diverted through canals to irrigate cotton and rice fields. By the 2000s, the sea level had dropped by more than 20 meters, the water had become very salty, and the fish had almost disappeared. In Nurmatov's opinion, the wasteful use of water on the fields led to the destruction of the sea.

The lesson of this remarkable but terrifying book is that it is people themselves who decide to change nature, and people who are able to save it. With hope, the author also tells the story of the Kokaral Dam, built in 2005 to save the Small Aral. The book is skillfully written, and everyone who loves nature should read it.

SOURCE 3. Popular science magazine article — “Was cotton alone to blame for drying up the Aral?” (sciencenow.uz/aral-climate)
Author: Botir Qodirov, science writer

In 2009, geographer Akmal Nurmatov published the book “The Dried-Up Sea.” In it, he also told the history of the fishing towns on the Aral coast, Moynaq and Aralsk.

After the book came out, a heated debate began. Some scientists questioned Nurmatov's theory about what happened to the Aral. They agree that the amount of river water reaching the Aral fell sharply after the 1960s, that is, after the period when the Moynaq cannery was at its peak. However, they disagree with Nurmatov about the cause of the decrease in water.

Recently, two scientists — hydrologist Laylo Karimova and climatologist Sardor Yoldoshev — announced a new theory. In their view, the main cause is the climate becoming drier: there has been less snow and rain in the mountains where the rivers begin, and in hot years more water has evaporated from rivers and fields. As a result, the rivers have carried much less water to the sea than before. The scientists believe that the Aral also became shallower naturally several times in the past.

In summer, the air temperature on the Aral coast rises above 40 °C, and in such heat a great deal of water evaporates from an open water surface. To support their theory, Karimova and Yoldoshev point to the remains of the 14th-century Kerderi Mausoleum, found in 2001 on the dried-up seabed: this means that in the Middle Ages the sea level was much lower than in 1960. Of course, they admit that irrigation also played a role in the drying of the Aral. But they consider the climate to be even more to blame.

Note: the blog, book, review, article and the people in them were invented for learning purposes. The information about the port of Moynaq and its ship graveyard, the area of the Aral in 1960, the Kokaral Dam and the Kerderi Mausoleum is real.

s0041: Sort the sentences in a review into facts (information that can be checked) and opinions (the author's judgments)
s0042: Ask of each sentence: “Can this be checked and proven?” If it contains judgment words (tragic, skillfully, should), it is an opinion.

Based on Source 2 (the review). Decide whether each of the following sentences from the review is a fact or an opinion.
1) The book describes several lakes and rivers that have changed dramatically because of human activity.
2) One of the most tragic examples in the book is the Aral Sea.
3) Starting in the 1960s, a large part of the water of the two rivers was diverted to irrigate fields.
4) In 1960, the Aral was the fourth-largest lake in the world.
5) The book is skillfully written, and everyone who loves nature should read it.
Which row gives the correct answers?
s0048: 1) the content of the book — can be checked → fact
s0049: You can open the book and see which lakes it describes — so this is a fact.
s0051: Each person judges for themselves which example is the most tragic; this is the reviewer's opinion.
s0053: The diversion of water for irrigation and the size of the lake can be checked with documents and measurements.
s0055: This is the reviewer's judgment and recommendation; it cannot be proven.
s0056: Answer: A) fact, opinion, fact, fact, opinion
s0057: So the correct answer is option A.
s0058: The words “most tragic” in sentence 2 are a judgment — this is an opinion. It is a mistake to think it is a fact just because the topic is serious.
s0059: Sentence 1 describes the content of the book and can be checked by reading it — it is a fact, not an opinion.
s0060: “The fourth-largest lake” in sentence 4 is the result of a measurement (area), not a judgment — it is a fact.
s0061: When separating facts from opinions, pay attention to judgment and recommendation words such as “most,” “remarkable,” “should” and “skillfully.”

Scenario. During the fall break, you visited your aunt, who lives in a village in the Namangan region. Your aunt keeps hens and chicks in her yard. She told you that once, when her chicks got sick, an online forum for poultry keepers was very helpful, and she showed you the conversation.

Website: “Backyard Poultry Health” — an online forum for poultry keepers (backyardpoultry.uz/forum)
Sections: About us | Forum | Photos
Topic: “Can I give my chicks an antibiotic meant for people?”

Dilfuza_88 (TOPIC STARTER) — November 14, 19:05
Hello! Yesterday three of my six 3-week-old chicks started sneezing, their eyes are watery, and one of them did not eat any grain at all today. I have an antibiotic at home that I take myself. Can I crush it and add it to the chicks' water? The district veterinary clinic is closed until Monday, and the emergency number is not answering. I'm afraid the other chicks will catch it too, and I need to do something for them before Monday. Thanks in advance!

Nilufar79 — November 14, 19:24
I think you shouldn't rush. Last year my neighbor gave her ducks her own medicine, and the ducks got even worse. Since then, I give my birds any medicine only after a vet tells me to.

Mohira — November 14, 19:40
Last spring my chicks were sneezing in exactly the same way. I crushed a little of the antibiotic I had at home and added it to their water, and they got better in two days! Just don't give them too much — an overdose can be harmful. I hope your chicks get well soon!

Poultry_Bazaar — November 14, 20:02
Hi! Don't miss our big discounts on feed, vitamins and equipment for poultry! This week, all products are 30 percent off!

Bobur_T — November 14, 20:15
My hens have stopped laying eggs as winter approaches. Does anyone have any advice?

Farhod_vet — November 14, 20:48
Hello, Dilfuza! I am a veterinarian specializing in poultry diseases. Do not give your chicks medicine made for people on your own: its ingredients and dose are not designed for birds. Veterinary pharmacies sell special medicines for chicks. According to the handbook “Poultry Diseases,” such a medicine is added to the drinking water, and the amount is calculated from the chicks' live weight: it states exactly how many milligrams to give per kilogram of body weight. For now, separate the sick chicks from the healthy ones and keep them in a warm, dry place. On Monday, be sure to show them to your vet. I hope they recover!

Note: the forum and its users are invented. Give animals any medicine only on a vet's advice.

Scenario. In a small café in Tashkent, three friends — Jasur, Malika and Sardor — noticed a sign on the door: “Dear guests! From now on, we will add oat milk instead of cow's milk to our drinks.” The friends became curious and searched for information about cow's milk on their phones. Jasur found the first page, and a little later Sardor showed his friends a second article.

SOURCE 1. Website of “Oqsoy Dairy Farm” (oqsoydairy.uz) — About us | Products | Healthy eating

The benefits of milk: countless!

“Oqsoy” dairy products contain substances that are important for the body: calcium, protein, vitamins B2 and B12, potassium and phosphorus. These substances make “Oqsoy” products an important part of a healthy diet. Having “Oqsoy” milk, yogurt and strained yogurt every day is the easiest way to get the vitamins and minerals your body needs.

“Oqsoy” products help you lose weight and maintain a healthy weight. They strengthen bones and teeth and improve heart health. A glass of “Oqsoy” milk is a treasure of vitamins, minerals and health!

According to pediatrician Rano Aliyeva, PhD in medicine, milk brings together many substances the body needs. The Association of Dairy Producers also supports this view and stresses that many health experts agree:

SOURCE 2. Article on the “Healthy Life” health portal — “Is it time to say ‘no’ to milk?”
Author: health writer and doctor N. Ganiyeva

In Uzbekistan, milk and dairy products are an essential part of every meal: tea with milk in the morning, yogurt at lunch, ayran in the evening. We have grown up hearing, “If you drink milk, your bones will be strong.” However, in recent years, more and more researchers have begun to question this belief.

For many years, milk producers have promoted drinking several glasses of milk a day. But a number of studies in the past decade have cast doubt on milk's ability to strengthen bones and on other claims. The results may surprise you.

One such study was published in 2014 in the respected “British Medical Journal.” More than 100 thousand people in Sweden were followed for 11–20 years. In women who drank a lot of milk, bone fractures did not decrease — on the contrary, they were slightly more common. In addition, among men and women who drank a lot of milk, the proportion who died during the study period was also higher.

According to scientists' estimates, in about two-thirds of the world's adults, the ability to digest lactose — milk sugar — decreases with age. In such people, drinking milk can cause bloating and stomach pain.

Of course, these are serious claims, and many more studies are needed to confirm them. The authors of the study themselves stressed that the results of an observational study do not prove cause and effect. However, there is growing evidence that milk is not as healthy as we thought. If these claims become undeniable facts, it may be time to say “no” to cow's milk.

Note: the “Oqsoy” farm, the association, the doctors and the “Healthy Life” portal are invented. The information about the 2014 Swedish study and about lactose is real.
